shortDescription: Retrieve a list of files from particular repository of a Bitbucket Server based on specific criteria

options.name: at
options.description: The commit ID or ref (e.g. a branch or tag) to read a file at. If not specified the default branch will be used instead.

options.name: grep
options.description: Python regex pattern to search for in each file selected from repository to form the final list of files. Files are selected based on C(patterns) option. Combined outcome of C(patterns) and C(grep) options form the final list of files returned by this module. If not specified, search will not be executed.

options.name: password
options.description: Password used for authentication. This is only needed when not using I(token). Required when I(username) is provided.

options.name: patterns
options.description: List of Python regex patterns to search for in file names on a Bitbucket Server repository. The patterns restrict the list of files to be returned to those whose basenames match at least one of the patterns specified. Multiple patterns can be specified using a list. This parameter expects a list, which can be either comma separated or YAML. If any of the patterns contain a comma, make sure to put them in a list to avoid splitting the patterns in undesirable ways. Defaults to '.+'.

options.name: retries
options.description: Number of retries to call Bitbucket API URL before failure.

options.name: sleep
options.description: Number of seconds to sleep between API retries.

options.name: token
options.description: Token parameter for authentication. This is only needed when not using I(username) and I(password).

options.name: use_proxy
options.description: If C(no), it will not use a proxy, even if one is defined in an environment variable on the target hosts.

options.name: username
options.description: Username used for authentication. This is only needed when not using I(token). Required when I(password) is provided.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If C(no), SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only set to C(no) used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.
